title: A Moment Unspoken
content:
Yashwanth glanced at the clock hanging on the wall and smiled.

"It's already quarter past one," he said. "I think we should continue the story tomorrow."

Siddu looked at him for a moment before nodding.

"Yeah... I think that's better."

Sneha agreed as well.

"Good night."

She walked toward her room.

As soon as the door closed, Siddu looked at Yashwanth and quietly said,

"Thanks."

Yashwanth smiled knowingly.

"No worries."

He had noticed something Sneha hadn't.

As Siddu narrated his past, the emotions he had buried for years had slowly begun to surface again. His expressions were becoming heavier with every memory.

"If he continues tonight," Yashwanth thought, "he won't be able to hide his pain."

That was the real reason he had stopped the story.

The house gradually fell silent.

Within minutes, all three of them drifted off to sleep.

The next morning, the first rays of sunlight slipped through the windows.

After getting ready, the three of them spent the morning exploring the peaceful streets of Dagshai once again.

Sneha couldn't help smiling.

"I don't think I'll ever get tired of this place."

Yashwanth laughed.

"That's the magic of Dagshai."

After spending a few more hours there, Yashwanth checked his watch.

"Siddu, I have some work to finish, so I'll leave now."

Before getting into his vehicle, he added,

"And don't forget to visit Mussoorie before leaving."

Siddu smiled.

"I won't."

The two friends hugged each other before Yashwanth departed.

A little while later, Siddu and Sneha booked a cab and continued their journey toward Mussoorie.

The winding mountain roads stretched endlessly ahead.

The gentle rocking of the cab and the cool breeze entering through the window slowly made Siddu feel sleepy.

Within a few minutes, he had fallen asleep.

Sneha had planned to ask him to continue the story during the journey.

But when she turned toward him...

She realized he was sleeping peacefully.

She smiled softly.

For a few moments, she simply kept looking at him.

The sunlight falling across the side of his face...

His calm expression...

His slightly messy hair moving with the breeze...

For some reason...

He looked even more handsome in his peaceful sleep.

Without realizing it, she leaned a little closer.

Her heartbeat began to race.

"What am I doing?" she asked herself.

But her heart refused to listen.

Almost unconsciously...

She leaned closer until only a few inches separated them.

Before she could stop herself, she gently kissed Siddu on the cheek.

The moment her lips touched his skin...

She froze.

Her own actions shocked her.

"Why did I do that?"

Before she could move away, Siddu suddenly stirred.

Feeling something soft brush against his cheek, he slowly opened his eyes.

He blinked in confusion and looked around.

Then his eyes met Sneha's.

"What happened?" he asked.

Sneha quickly turned her face toward the window.

"N-Nothing."

Her voice betrayed her nervousness.

Siddu touched his cheek.

For a brief moment, he felt as though something warm had touched him.

He frowned slightly before smiling to himself.

"Maybe... I was dreaming."

Siddu leaned back against the seat once again and slowly closed his eyes.

Within a few moments...

He had fallen asleep once more.

Sneha quietly looked at him.

A gentle smile appeared on her lips.

Almost without realizing it, she slowly raised her hand and brushed away a few strands of hair that had fallen across his forehead.

"This is getting dangerous..." she whispered to herself.

She immediately withdrew her hand.

Her heart refused to calm down.

She looked out through the window as the mountains rushed past.

The cool breeze touched her face, but it couldn't cool the warmth spreading through her cheeks.

For the first time...

She wasn't thinking about Siddu's past.

She wasn't thinking about Shreya.

She wasn't even thinking about the story he had been telling.

She was only thinking about the strange feeling growing inside her heart.

Until now, she had convinced herself that she only admired Siddu.

That she simply respected him.

That she enjoyed listening to him.

But after what had just happened...

Those excuses no longer made sense.

She gently touched her own lips.

A shy smile slowly spread across her face.

"For the first time..."

She stopped asking herself whether she liked Siddu.

Deep inside...

Her heart had already answered the question long before her mind was ready to accept it.

Outside the window, the winding roads of the Himalayas stretched endlessly into the distance.

Neither of them realized it yet...

But just as their journey toward Mussoorie had begun...

A new journey had quietly begun inside Sneha's heart as well.
